Nervous System
The brain is one of the sites shown to be particularly sensitive to zinc deﬁciency during fetal development, with neural tube defects
and other disorders being found. Although this work was performed with animals, a similar relationship appears likely with
humans. Zinc is distributed throughout the brain, but greater concentrations are found within the hippocampus. Here a brain-
speciﬁc transporter, ZnT-3, concentrates zinc in vesicles within glutamatergic neurons. It is co-secreted with the neurotransmitter
and appears to serve as a modulator of neurotransmission. Very high concentrations of zinc (>100 µM) are found within the
synaptic cleft during this process. In addition, brain injury, resulting from ischemia or trauma causes the release of massive amounts
of zinc, which is thought to be responsible for the resultant cell death.
